headline: PRESS RELEASE ON 393rd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE
fullText:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat

PRESS RELEASE ON 393rd REPORT OF THE DEPARTMENT-RELATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE

12 AUG 2026 10:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture headed by Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha, M.P., Rajya Sabha, presented its 393rd Report on “From Manuscript to Mission: Preserving, Mapping and Sustaining India’s Cultural Heritage in the Age of Artificial Intelligence” on Wednesday, the 12th August, 2026.

The Report was adopted by the Committee on 11th August, 2026. The Key Recommendations/Observations made by the Committee in this Report are enclosed.

The full Report is available on the website of Rajya Sabha https://sansad.in/rs -→Committees→Department related RS→Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture-→ Report

THE THREE HUNDRED NINETY THIRD REPORT OF DEPARTMENT-REL koi ATED PARLIAMENTARY STANDING COMMITTEE ON TRANSPORT, TOURISM AND CULTURE

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Enlarge the digitisation standard into a complete capture standard, settled in consultation with scholars, scientists and custodians and in force before the contracts reach full scale: a multispectral recovery tier for damaged and overwritten folios; surface-relief imaging as the standard for palm leaf; a materials record for significant manuscripts; and a dating protocol anchored at Indian accelerator laboratories with margins stated on the record. (Paragraph 5.1.2)

2. Institute, with the national scientific departments, a research and challenge programme to read manuscripts that cannot be opened, beginning with a census of fused and fire-damaged holdings. (Paragraph 5.2.2)

3. Build the national reading workforce: the Akshar Mitra citizen platform with two independent checks on every page and permanent contributor credit; the university compact under which unedited manuscripts become dissertation editions recognised as research of the first rank; and published priority lists so that effort chases textual value. (Paragraph 5.3.2)

4. Release every publicly funded page and verified transcription as an open national library of training pages with an annual public benchmark, and employ federated learning so that restricted collections contribute without an image leaving custody. (Paragraph 5.4.2)

5. Publish the open index of persons, places and works of the corpus, the time-layered atlas of Indian knowledge built upon it, and the register of scribal hands. (Paragraph 5.5.2)

6. Extract the astronomical and weather observations of the corpus, with the national scientific agencies, as open national datasets for Indian science. (Paragraph 5.6.2)

7. Constitute the standing programme to reunite the scattered corpus: a common catalogue of dispersed and overseas holdings; exchange of images; virtual rebinding by computer matching of leaves and hands; and the identification of Indian manuscripts held overseas, the acquisition of digital copies of them and steps to bring back originals where return can be secured, with reunified treasures proposed for the Memory of the World register. (Paragraph 5.7.2)

8. Build, with the Ministry of Ayush, the concordance connecting manuscript formulations to the national terminologies and the statutory pharmacopoeia. (Paragraph 5.8.2)

9. Build the Repository's architecture of trust: the international image interoperability framework as the access standard; community access protocols under which every custodian chooses, item by item, what is shown; and an embedded credential in every machine-produced rendering, with the Ministry advocating its preservation with the major platforms. (Paragraph 5.9.2)

10. Serve the living inheritance: oral heritage recorded through Indian-language speech recognition, beginning with the fewest surviving bearers; fonts, keyboards and voices for every encoded script, freely downloadable and offered to the major operating systems; and the technique of the last masters recorded in three dimensions, with personal designation, lifetime grant and successor duties. (Paragraph 5.10.2)

11. Put the map to work: the cultural and manuscript layers on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan and in district planning; knowledge tourism circuits designed from them; and the mapped artisan joined to commerce through the Open Network for Digital Commerce with authenticity credentials linked to the map. (Paragraph 5.11.2)

Establish the guardianship framework: the machine-graded register of manuscripts at risk with preservation kits and connected loggers for custodians; district salvage annexes wired into the national alerting infrastructure with cultural first-aid training; and a published preservation architecture of distributed copies and a deep archive on century-lasting media. (Paragraph 5.12.2)

headline: India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) sign Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) sign Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement

Union Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Balanced and Equitable India–SACU Trade Agreement

India Can Support Affordable Medicines, IT Talent and Global Supply Chain Integration in SACU Region: Shri Goyal

Negotiations to cover eight important chapters, including trade in goods, market access for goods and rules of origin: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal

12 AUG 2026 9:36PM by PIB Delhi

India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) today signed the Terms of Reference (ToR) for negotiations towards a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) between India and SACU at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The signing marks an important step towards strengthening trade and economic engagement between India and the SACU Member States.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called for a balanced, fair and equitable trade agreement between India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), emphasising that the partnership can help diversify markets and create opportunities for both sides to prosper. Shri Goyal said India can play an important role in supplying affordable medicines and supporting the development of new talent in the IT sector in the SACU region. Shri Goyal added that India can also help integrate SACU countries into global supply chains in areas where their businesses are competitive and where skills and talent can be developed or are already available.

The Minister stated that India’s engagement with Southern Africa is rooted in a longstanding partnership of equals and extends well beyond trade. He recalled that Southern Africa occupies a special place in India’s national memory, noting that “India’s relationship with Southern Africa did not begin with commerce. It began with conscience.” Recalling Mahatma Gandhi, he also highlighted India’s support for the peoples of Southern Africa in their struggle against apartheid.

Shri Goyal underscored that the negotiations seek to provide preferential market access to an already established commercial relationship, with significant complementarities in engineering goods and machinery, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, textiles, agriculture and agri-processing. He called upon the negotiating teams to proceed with urgency and stressed the importance of translating the agreed Terms of Reference into a concrete process towards early finalisation of the India–SACU PTA. He further noted, “What we sign today does not by itself lower a single tariff or clear a single container. Only a final agreement will do that,” and called for an early conclusion of the PTA.

The signing ceremony was attended by Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada, senior officials from the Government of India and the SACU delegation.

Executive Director, Ministry of International Relations and Trade, Government of the Republic of Namibia, Ms. Ndiitah Nghipondoka-Robiati welcomed the signing of the ToR as an important milestone in formalising SACU–India engagement and providing structure, transparency and predictability to the forthcoming negotiations. Highlighting India’s importance as a strategic partner and a pillar of South–South cooperation, she noted the longstanding relationship between India and Africa through trade, investment, capacity building and development cooperation. She emphasised that SACU attaches real importance to an outcome that is balanced and takes into account the different levels of development among the Parties, particularly the interests and development needs of SACU Member States, including its Least Developed Countries and Small and Vulnerable Economies.

Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, addressing the gathering, said that this is India’s first ToR signing with the African region and noted SACU’s significance as the oldest customs union in the world. He stated that the PTA is envisaged to cover eight important chapters, including trade in goods and market access for goods; rules of origin and origin procedures; customs procedures and trade facilitation; trade remedies, including a bilateral safeguard mechanism; sanitary and phytosanitary measures; technical barriers to trade; dispute settlement; and legal and horizontal provisions.

The signing of the ToR reflects the shared commitment of India and SACU to advance mutually beneficial trade relations and lays the foundation for negotiations towards a balanced, mutually beneficial and development-oriented PTA.

Abhishek Dayal/Shabbir Azad/Anushka Pandey

(Release ID: 2298681)

headline: LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SHRI KOVIND’S STORY AS AN ENDURING SOURCE OF “INSPIRATION FOR GENERATIONS”
fullText:
Lok Sabha Secretariat

LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SHRI KOVIND’S STORY AS AN ENDURING SOURCE OF “INSPIRATION FOR GENERATIONS”

PRIME MINISTER RELEASES AUTOBIOGRAPHY OF FORMER PRESIDENT SHRI RAM NATH KOVIND

SHRI KOVIND’S AUTOBIOGRAPHY PRESENTS AN EXTRAORDINARY JOURNEY OF STRUGGLE, RESOLVE, AND ACHIEVEMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

SHRI KOVIND UPHELD CONSTITUTIONAL TRADITIONS WITH UNWAVERING COMMITMENT TO SOCIAL HARMONY AND INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

DURING COVID-19 PANDEMIC, SHRI KOVIND INSTILLED COURAGE AND CONFIDENCE AMONG PEOPLE AND MADE RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN MORE ACCESSIBLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

12 AUG 2026 9:08PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla was present on the occasion and described the release of the book as a matter of great pride and significance.

Speaking at the distinguished gathering, Shri Birla observed that the autobiography of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind, an embodiment of high constitutional ideals, presents an extraordinary journey of determination, struggle, and achievement. Recalling the challenges of Shri Kovind’s early life, including the difficulties he faced in pursuing his education, he said that his journey from a humble and economically disadvantaged background to the highest constitutional office of the country reflects his extraordinary resolve and serves as an enduring source of inspiration for generations to come.

The Lok Sabha Speaker noted that Shri Kovind’s unwavering commitment to constitutional values enabled him to leave an indelible mark as an advocate. His tenure as a Member of Parliament, he said, was marked by dedication to the welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, social justice, and probity in public life.

Referring to Shri Kovind’s tenure as Governor, Shri Birla mentioned that he provided a new direction to transparency, quality, and technological innovation in higher education. As President of India, he upheld the constitutional traditions of Indian democracy and demonstrated an unwavering commitment to social harmony and inclusive development. Further, through his visits to several countries, he also contributed to strengthening India’s international diplomatic relations, he added.

Shri Birla also mentioned that during the challenging period of the COVID-19 pandemic, Shri Kovind instilled courage, unity, and confidence among the people of the country and made the Rashtrapati Bhavan more accessible to the public. He described this as one of Shri Kovind’s significant achievements.

The Lok Sabha Speaker added that even after demitting the office of President, Shri Kovind continues to contribute to the nation, the Constitution, and society through his vast experience, reflections on public life, and commitment to social justice. Shri Birla expressed confidence that ‘Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles’ would bring before readers important episodes from Shri Kovind’s life and inspire them to play a purposive role in public life. He concluded by extending his warm congratulations and best wishes to Shri Ram Nath Kovind on the publication of the book.

headline: Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) and NITI Aayog Sign Statement of Intent to Advance Multilingual AI for Inclusive Governance
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) and NITI Aayog Sign Statement of Intent to Advance Multilingual AI for Inclusive Governance

Partnership to Enable Voice-First, Multilingual AI for Citizen-Centric Governance and Public Service Delivery

12 AUG 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, and NITI Aayog, Government of India, have signed a Statement of Intent (SoI) to collaborate on advancing multilingual, voice-first AI solutions for inclusive governance and citizen-centric public service delivery through the BHASHINI for Seva/Sanchalan initiative.

The SoI was signed by Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, and Shri Shoyabahmed Kalal, Director, NITI Aayog.

The collaboration aims to leverage BHASHINI's multilingual AI ecosystem to enable more inclusive and accessible governance by integrating AI-powered language technologies across NITI Aayog's digital platforms and services. The partnership will facilitate access to government information and services in citizens' preferred Indian languages, strengthen communication between government and citizens, and promote multilingual operations across public service delivery.

Under the SoI, both organisations will collaborate across BHASHINI Udyat, BHASHINI Mitra, BHASHINI AppMitra, BHASHINI Sahayogi and BHASHINI Pravakta. The partnership will facilitate multilingual access to NITI Aayog services through BHASHINI's language translation APIs and reference applications, support the development and continuous improvement of translation models, and enable the integration of language technologies into digital platforms, document management systems and communication workflows.

The collaboration will also support the development of reference applications and voice bots for specific NITI Aayog sectors and strengthen language technology for specialised terminology and sector-specific requirements. Through BHASHINI Sahayogi, the partnership will leverage BhashaDaan for the collection, curation and dissemination of linguistic data, with NITI Aayog officials and citizens encouraged to contribute text, audio and video samples.

Through BHASHINI Pravakta, the two organisations will work towards expanding awareness and adoption of BHASHINI's services, tools and resources across districts, supported by training, technical assistance and resources to ensure that multilingual digital solutions remain accessible to users with varying levels of digital literacy.

The collaboration also builds on NITI TARA (Toolkit for Analysis, Review & Action), which is transforming data into action at the grassroots. With 200+ capacity-building sessions conducted across the country, NITI TARA has empowered over 4,000 officials from districts and blocks to leverage data-driven insights for evidence-based decision-making. Through interactive multi-sectoral dashboards, intuitive visualisations and collaborative planning tools, the platform is simplifying reviews, strengthening inter-departmental coordination and enabling more effective governance.

An important component of this ecosystem is SMRITI (System for Meeting Recording, Information & Transcription Interface), developed in collaboration with BHASHINI. By automating meeting minutes and enabling multilingual translation, SMRITI is enhancing operational efficiency while making governance more inclusive at the last mile.

The collaboration is expected to contribute to bridging language barriers, enabling bidirectional communication between government and the public, and promoting multilingual operations for more inclusive public service delivery.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is India's national platform for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. Today, BHASHINI powers over 800 government websites, has enabled more than 9 billion cumulative AI inferences, processes over 24 million AI inferences daily, and supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, making Digital Public Infrastructure more accessible through Language AI.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app via video conferencing; the app was developed to interconnect libraries in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat
fullText:
Ministry of Home Affairs

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah launches the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app via video conferencing; the app was developed to interconnect libraries in the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat

‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ is a new initiative; its objective is to establish a library in every village to encourage children to read

752 libraries have joined the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app so far

Four libraries containing 2.80 lakh books have been linked with these rural libraries

The process of opening 63 libraries—each stocked with five to six thousand books—has begun across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies

Home Minister has personally prepared a list of books for libraries—books that will spark an interest in reading among children and inspire them to dive into the vast ocean of knowledge

Vans provided through the MPLADs will visit villages every fortnight to collect previously distributed books and deliver books registered on the app to village libraries

12 AUG 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today launched the 'Gramin Gyan Setu' app developed to integrate the libraries of Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency of Gujarat through video conferencing.

Addressing the event virtually, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah noted that today marks the birth anniversary of S.R. Ranganathan. He stated that the entire nation is celebrating the birth anniversary of Padma Shri Ranganathan as National Library Day, and that a new idea and concept—‘Gramin Gyan Setu’—has been launched in his Lok Sabha constituency. Shri Shah stated that the objective is to establish a library in every village—located centrally and near the school—to encourage children to engage with reading and learning. He noted that approximately 63 libraries have already been set up. Initiatives have been launched to open small libraries, each housing five to six thousand books, across all villages in the Gandhinagar, Kalol, and Sanand assembly constituencies. Union Home Minister mentioned that he personally curated a list of books for these multi-purpose, multi-dimensional libraries—books designed to spark an interest in reading among children and gradually inspire them to immerse themselves in the vast ocean of knowledge. Additionally, the libraries will stock books beneficial for the career development of adolescents and youth, as well as resources for state and national-level competitive examinations. Arrangements have also been made to ensure the availability of books covering the history of Gujarat, the history of the nation, the story of the freedom struggle, and the Revolution of 1857 right within the village.

Shri Amit Shah stated that cultivating a reading habit in children is not possible without encouragement from parents; however, for children who are motivated to study, four libraries—collectively housing 2.80 lakh books that will benefit them in the future—have been linked to these rural libraries. Union Home Minister mentioned that he has facilitated this service by arranging vans using his MP Local Area Development (MPLAD) funds. These vans will visit the villages every fortnight to collect previously issued books and deliver books registered on the app to the village libraries. He noted that children who are accustomed to visiting libraries containing 6,000 to 7,000 books will now have access to a collection of 2.80 lakh books.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that while he had originally proposed the idea, Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel and the Gujarat government have integrated it with a new scientific approach. He noted that 752 libraries are now connected to the ‘Gramin Gyan Setu’ app. He emphasized that without study, it is impossible to gain even basic knowledge, let alone achieve mastery in any subject. He added that as individuals transition from childhood to adolescence, then to youth, and finally to adulthood, guidance from competent librarians regarding studies and their various dimensions can enable libraries to play a pivotal role in shaping citizens who are valuable to the nation.

Shri Amit Shah stated that the Mahatma Gandhi Library in Mansa has been linked to this library-related scheme. He mentioned that at the Mahatma Gandhi Library, he acquired basic knowledge across various subjects and gained in-depth understanding of some over a period of 16 years. After moving from Mansa to Ahmedabad, he became associated with the Gujarat Vidyapith library. He noted that Kakasaheb Kalelkar had created the Gujarat Vidyapith library as a means for many young people—like himself—to dive into the ocean of knowledge. The urge to gather information on every subject evolved into a habit, which subsequently transformed into a practice of study. He remarked that it was this practice of study that enabled him to contribute to a specific field, and the library played a pivotal role in this process.

Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that these libraries and books have now been made available to the youth through the ‘hub-and-spoke’ model. While such facilities did not exist in his time, this program is now scientifically accessible to the current generation. He expressed his aim to have various institutions—such as Sastu Sahitya Mandal, Gita Press, the Bhupen Hazarika Institute, and the Thiruvalluvar Institute—connect online with libraries in Gujarat’s Gandhinagar district and at the state level. He expressed confidence that this facility would become available to students and readers through the use of technology.

Shri Amit Shah urged housewives across the country and the state to make productive use of their spare time by acquiring knowledge on various subjects and encouraging their children to study.

headline: National Commission for Scheduled Castes submits Annual Report-2024–25 to Hon’ble President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu
fullText:

National Commission for Scheduled Castes submits Annual Report-2024–25 to Hon’ble President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu

headline: Union Health Minister Shri Nadda interacts with MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha to strengthen efforts towards TB Mukt Bharat
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Minister Shri Nadda interacts with MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha to strengthen efforts towards TB Mukt Bharat

MPs commit to intensify awareness, strengthen oversight and mobilise communities for TB elimination

Shri Nadda calls for sustained parliamentary engagement and district-level oversight to accelerate TB elimination

Parliamentarians from Jharkhand and Odisha unite to strengthen last-mile TB services

12 AUG 2026 8:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda today interacted with Members of Parliament from Jharkhand and Odisha on the sidelines of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, as part of the Government’s continued engagement with parliamentarians to accelerate efforts towards a TB Mukt Bharat. Smt. Anupriya Patel, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare & Chemicals and Fertilizers, and Shri Sanjay Seth, Union Minister of State for Defence, also participated in the interaction.

The interaction, held under the theme “Parliamentarians Championing a TB Mukt Bharat”, brought together Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs from both States across party lines, reflecting a shared commitment to strengthening the fight against tuberculosis through political leadership, community participation and last-mile delivery of services.

The interaction reviewed progress under the recently concluded 100-Day TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, which was implemented in two phases to accelerate TB elimination efforts. The second phase, launched on March 24, 2026, covered nearly 1.58 lakh high-risk villages and urban wards across the country and concluded in July 2026.

During the campaign, over 2.2 crore vulnerable individuals were screened, more than 7 lakh new TB cases were detected, and 1.97 lakh asymptomatic TB cases were identified—cases that may otherwise have remained undetected. The intensified case-finding approach has demonstrated the importance of proactive screening, particularly among vulnerable and high-risk populations.

India has made significant progress in TB elimination, recording a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024, nearly twice the global pace, along with a 92% treatment success rate, according to the WHO Global TB Report 2025. The intensified focus on early detection, treatment and patient support is central to sustaining this momentum.

Jharkhand and Odisha remain important focus States given the presence of several TB risk factors, including mining and industrial belts, occupational dust exposure, migrant and tribal populations, malnutrition, urban slums, comorbidities, tobacco and alcohol consumption, and informal and labour settlements.

During the 100-Day campaign, Jharkhand notified 16,754 TB patients, including 4,574 asymptomatic cases, while Odisha notified 15,268 patients, including 3,514 asymptomatic cases.

The States adopted targeted strategies to take screening and care closer to vulnerable populations, including through Ayushman Arogya Shivirs in urban slums, construction sites, migrant clusters and mining areas.

The technological expansion of India’s TB programme has further strengthened these efforts. Molecular testing capacity has expanded from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 machines, while nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units are now supporting active case finding in the field.

Shri Nadda emphasised the importance of sustained political and administrative engagement in achieving the goal of a TB Mukt Bharat. He highlighted innovative case-finding strategies, early diagnosis, patient-centric care and community participation as critical pillars of India’s accelerated TB elimination strategy.

He called upon parliamentarians to play an active role in their constituencies by engaging with District Collectors and health facilities, reviewing the availability and quality of TB services, and supporting efforts for early diagnosis and treatment. He also stressed the need for continued public engagement and social mobilisation to ensure that TB elimination becomes a sustained Jan Andolan.

The participating MPs from Jharkhand and Odisha reaffirmed their commitment to intensifying awareness and stigma-reduction campaigns, promoting Ni-kshay Shivirs for early detection, particularly among vulnerable populations, and strengthening supportive supervision of TB services at district and block levels.

The parliamentarians also committed to mobilising communities and organisations to provide nutritional, psychosocial and livelihood support to people affected by TB, thereby strengthening the patient-centric approach to TB care.

The interaction is part of a series of consultations being held by the Union Health Minister with Members of Parliament from different States to strengthen collective ownership and a whole-of-government approach towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat.

Shri Nadda expressed confidence that sustained engagement by parliamentarians, State and district administrations, healthcare workers and communities will further accelerate progress towards TB elimination, with the conclusion of the 100-Day campaign serving as a platform for deeper and continued action at the grassroots level.

Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava highlighted the focused efforts being undertaken in Jharkhand and Odisha to address TB among vulnerable and priority populations, including communities in mining and industrial areas, migrant and tribal populations, urban settlements, and groups requiring additional support due to factors such as malnutrition and comorbidities. She emphasised the importance of targeted screening, early detection and accessible patient-centric care to further strengthen TB elimination efforts in both States. She shared that Jharkhand notified 16,754 TB patients during the 100-Day campaign, including 4,574 asymptomatic cases, while Odisha notified 15,268 patients, including 3,514 asymptomatic cases. She emphasised the need for continued intensified screening and targeted interventions among vulnerable populations to sustain the momentum towards TB elimination.

Additional Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik highlighted the technological foundation underpinning India’s intensified TB case-finding efforts. She noted that India has expanded molecular testing capacity from a few hundred machines a decade ago to more than 9,000 machines, supported by nearly 3,000 AI-enabled handheld X-ray units deployed in the field.

She also presented an overview of Jharkhand and Odisha’s performance across key indicators, including TB notifications, treatment success, preventive therapy coverage and progress against national TB elimination benchmarks.

Smt. Patnaik highlighted that during the 100-Day campaign, both States adopted targeted strategies to take screening and care closer to vulnerable populations, including through Ayushman Arogya Shivirs in urban slums, construction sites, migrant clusters and mining areas. These approaches helped strengthen active case finding and bring TB services closer to communities that may otherwise face barriers in accessing diagnosis and treatment.

The collective commitment of the parliamentarians, State and district administrations, healthcare workers and communities is expected to further strengthen the national resolve towards achieving a TB Mukt Bharat.

Recognition highlights growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future

12 AUG 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

With an objective of creating opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future at the international level, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, has facilitated the selection of three Sanchar Mitras (youth volunteers) from India as Generation Connect Youth Envoys (GCYE) of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This comes as the global community celebrates International Youth Day 2026 under the theme “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations”. The Generation Connect community marked the occasion through the virtual “Passing the Torch: Connecting Generations of Digital Leaders” event today , bringing together the outgoing and incoming cohorts of Generation Connect Youth Envoys.

Ankit Kumar Pal from Delhi, Manish Kumar Mandal from Bengaluru and Susmita Sain from Guwahati have been selected as part of the third cohort of ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030 in recognition of their contribution under the Sanchar Mitra scheme of DoT. Their selection marks an important recognition of the growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future.

The Generation Connect Youth Envoys programme provides young people with opportunities to contribute to national, regional and global discussions and initiatives related to Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), digital transformation and inclusive digital development.

The initiative aligns closely with the objectives of the Sanchar Mitra Scheme, which seeks to engage young people in telecom and digital initiatives and provide them exposure to national and international platforms. The scheme also envisages opportunities for selected Sanchar Mitras to participate in global telecom platforms such as the ITU.

Following ITU’s invitation for nominations to the third cohort of Generation Connect Youth Envoys, the Department of Telecommunications initiated a process to identify suitable candidates from among Sanchar Mitras. The process sought candidates with demonstrated engagement in areas including youth-led initiatives, digital inclusion, ICT education and skills, research and technical activities, entrepreneurship and innovation, and community-level ICT initiatives.

The recognition also reflects India’s commitment to empowering young people as active contributors to the country’s digital transformation journey and strengthening youth participation in global conversations on technology, connectivity and inclusive digital development.

Through initiatives such as Sanchar Mitra and its engagement with global platforms including the ITU Generation Connect programme, the Department of Telecommunications continues to create opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future.

The Sanchar Mitra Scheme envisions to engage the Yuva Shakti- India’s youth, as catalysts for digital empowerment and societal outreach. The students nominated as Sanchar Mitra actively conduct awareness drives in communities, educational institutions, public spaces, etc., focusing on key telecom-related issues, like citizen-centric telecom services, prevention of telecom frauds and mobile security - promoting digital safety, and foster responsible telecom usage.

This scheme is open to students from those technical institutes that have active telecom, electronics, computers, cybersecurity or similar programs and have agreed to participate in the scheme.

The scheme has been implemented across all states/ UTs through the LSA field offices of DoT. More than 200 institutions are currently participating in it.

fullText:

National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services

12 AUG 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) today launched its e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services. Hon’ble President, NCLT, Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, inaugurated the services through video conferencing, marking another step towards making the Tribunal’s Registry more accessible and technology-enabled.

Speaking on the occasion, Justice Grewal said that the two services are intended to provide advocates, litigants and other stakeholders with convenient and faster access to judicial records and certified copies. The services form part of the Tribunal’s broader digital transformation, including the revamped NCLT website and the ongoing e-Courts 2.0 initiative.

The Hon’ble NCLT President also highlighted the measures undertaken to improve case management and reduce pendency. The NCLT has adopted a data-driven mechanism to monitor pendency across Benches. Based on the data so collated, workload was reviewed and redistributed, Special Benches were constituted wherever required, and efforts were made to maximise the available Court time.

These measures contributed to the approval of 78 resolution plans during April–June 2026, the highest first-quarter performance since the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, involving approximately ₹5,517.66 crore.

The NCLT has also issued detailed guidelines on registration and listing of cases, in consultation with the Bar, to ensure optimum utilisation of limited judicial resources.

Justice Grewal emphasised that while the Tribunal continues to face infrastructural and manpower constraints, sustained efforts are being made to reduce avoidable delays and improve efficiency.

The launch of the two services is part of the NCLT’s continuing endeavour to provide a more transparent, efficient and stakeholder-oriented system of justice delivery.

headline: The Government of India to launch the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the Union Territories of Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli
fullText:
Ministry of Company Affairs

The Government of India to launch the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the Union Territories of Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli

12 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India will launch the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) in the Union Territories of Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli on 14 August 2026. The launch will be graced by Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, Governor of Punjab and Administrator, U.T. Chandigarh, Shri Gulab Chand Kataria, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan; Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, and other dignitaries.

The launch of CBDC-based DBT under PMGKAY marks a significant milestone in India’s journey towards building a modern, transparent and technology-driven welfare delivery ecosystem.

Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli are set to become the first Union Territories in the country to operationalize food subsidy transfers to all eligible PMGKAY beneficiaries in the form of programmable Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC – Digital Rupee) tokens directly into their CBDC wallets.

Building on earlier pilot implementations in Puducherry and Gujarat, the rollout marks complete digital adoption and saturation of all eligible beneficiaries across the targeted Union Territories.

Under the CBDC-based DBT model, eligible PMGKAY beneficiaries will receive food subsidy directly into their CBDC wallets instead of conventional bank account transfers. The subsidy can then be used to purchase foodgrains from empanelled merchants through a secure, traceable and real-time digital payment mechanism.

The CBDC-enabled DBT model seeks to ensure transparent and end-to-end traceable delivery of public funds, while reducing leakages, diversion and cash handling associated with traditional subsidy delivery mechanisms. It will also facilitate instant and secure transfer of benefits to beneficiaries and promote financial inclusion through simple wallet-based transactions.

The initiative will further strengthen accountability and real-time monitoring of subsidy utilization and demonstrate the potential of the Digital Rupee for future payment systems.

The rollout is envisaged as a proof of concept for the nation and a scalable template for adoption by other States and Union Territories. It is expected to provide valuable operational experience regarding the integration of CBDC with welfare schemes and support the Government’s vision of strengthening Digital Public Infrastructure and delivering citizen-centric services through innovative technologies.

headline: India’s Infrastructure Transformation: From Connectivity to Capacity
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

India’s Infrastructure Transformation: From Connectivity to Capacity

12 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

Building the Foundation of Growth

India’s infrastructure landscape has undergone a major transformation over the past 12 years. From transport and logistics to housing and water, infrastructure development has moved towards integrated planning and large-scale expansion. This has strengthened connectivity, improved access to essential services and created the foundations for sustained economic growth. Public capital expenditure has risen from about ₹2 lakh crore in FY 2014–15 to ₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026–27, supporting this advancement.

A New Era of Rail Mobility

Indian Railways is moving towards faster, safer and more modern mobility. Electrification, advanced safety systems, high-speed rail and new-generation trains are reshaping the rail network.

Railway budget increased from ₹32,000 crore in 2014–15 to ₹2.78 lakh crore in FY2026–27.

Rail electrification increased from about 20% before 2014 to 99.6% by July 2026.

162 Vande Bharat, 2 Vande Bharat Sleeper Services and 72 Amrit Bharat services have improved connectivity and travel experience.

The Kavach Version 4.0 has been commissioned on 2,633 route km as of July 2026.

The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor is being developed over a 508 km route with a design speed of 350 kmph.

Of the 1,340 stations identified under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, redevelopment has been completed for 261 stations as on 18 July 2026.

First indigenously developed Hydrogen Fuel Cell Trainset has been launched in July 2026. It is a 10-coach train with capacity for around 2,600 passengers, running on the Jind–Sonipat section. It generates its own electricity onboard with water vapour and heat as the only by-product.

Roads and Highways Connecting India

A wider and more capable road network is bringing regions closer. The expansion of National Highways, rural roads and major corridors is enabling smoother movement of people and goods.

India has the world’s second-largest road network at 63.73 lakh km.

Length of national highways increased by about 61%, from 91,287 km in FY 14 to 1,46,572 km in March 2026.

The length of four-lane and above national highways increased from 18,371 km in 2014 to 45,516 km.

The length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km during 2000–2014 to 4.11 lakh km during 2014–2026 under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. Since September 2024, PMGSY-IV has been launched with an objective to provide connectivity to 25,000 unconnected habitations by the year 2029.

Under Bharatmala, 22,590 km of roads have been completed till 31 March 2026.

Bridges and Tunnels: Engineering New Frontiers

Engineering breakthroughs are overcoming some of India’s most demanding geographical challenges. These projects are opening new routes across difficult terrain.

Chenab Bridge (2025): World's highest railway arch bridge, standing 359 m above the Chenab River; 1,315 m steel structure strengthening Jammu–Srinagar connectivity.

Anji Khad Bridge (2025): India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, in Jammu & Kashmir.

Pamban Bridge (2025): India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge, connecting Rameswaram to the mainland; 2.07 km with a 72.5 m vertical lift span.

Z-Morh/Sonamarg Tunnel (2025): 12 km tunnel providing all-weather access through avalanche-prone terrain in J&K, improving movement towards Ladakh.

Sudarshan Setu (2024): 2.32 km bridge connecting Okha with Beyt Dwarka, Gujarat.

Atal Tunnel (2020): 9.02 km — world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet, connecting Manali and Lahaul-Spiti.

Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee Tunnel (2017): 9 km all-weather tunnel between Jammu and Srinagar, cutting travel time by ~2 hours.

Civil Aviation and Regional Air Access

Air connectivity is reaching more cities, towns and remote regions. The expansion of airports, UDAN routes and digital passenger services is making flying more accessible across the country.

UDAN connected 95 airports, heliports, and water aerodromes through 679 routes, benefiting over 1.68 crore passengers as on 15 July 2026.

Operational airports increased from 74 in 2014 to 165 in July 2026.

25 greenfield airports have been approved after 2014.

Digi Yatra is active at 38 airports. The app has enabled over 10 crore seamless journeys with over 2.4 crore downloads.

Modified UDAN has been approved in March 2026 for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 with an outlay of ₹28,840 crore, envisioning 100 new airports and 200 modern helipads to strengthen last-mile regional air connectivity.

Metro: The Rise of Mass Urban Transit

India’s urban mobility network is expanding in scale and scope. Metro connectivity now spans more cities, while innovative systems are opening new possibilities for urban transport.

Metro network expanded from 248 km in 2014 to over 1,155 km in 2026.

Cities with metro connectivity increased from 5 to 26, while daily ridership crossed 1.15 crore passengers.

Kolkata operationalised India’s first underwater metro tunnel in 2024.

Kochi operationalised India’s first Water Metro system with the first boat launched in December 2021.

India’s Maritime Momentum

India is strengthening its maritime backbone to support a growing economy and expanding trade. Investments in ports, waterways and maritime infrastructure are creating a more capable and connected ecosystem.

Major ports’ cargo handling capacity nearly doubled from 873 MMTPA in 2014 to 1,728 MMTPA in 2026.

Vessel turnaround time improved from 94 hours to 48.8 hours in 2025-26.

Major ports collectively handled 915.17 MT of cargo during FY 2025-26, increasing from 581 MT in FY 2014-15.

The Sagarmala Programme strengthened port-led development, coastal connectivity, and logistics integration.

National waterways increased from 5 in 2014 to 111 in 2026, of which 32 are operational.

India became the world's No. 1 ship-recycling nation in 2025, with its global share rising from 30.1% (2024) to 35.4% (2025) — recycling 2.99 million gross tons (GT), up nearly 60% from 1.86 million GT in 2024.

Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22nd as per the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) 2025, published by the World Bank.

Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) has been launched on 12 May 2026. It is a USD 1.5 billion domestic insurance pool with a sovereign guarantee of USD 1.4 billion (₹12,980 crore), covering Hull & Machinery, Cargo, Protection and Indemnity, and War risk for Indian-flagged/controlled vessels. As on 29th July 2026, a total of 1608 policies covering Cargo War risks and Hull War risks have been issued under the Pool.

Strengthening Logistics and Industrial Capacity

Infrastructure is increasingly being planned as an interconnected network supporting industry and trade. From GatiShakti to industrial corridors, the focus is on improving coordination, efficiency and manufacturing capacity.

PM GatiShakti National Master Plan integrated infrastructure planning across 58 Ministries and Departments using over 3,291 data layers.

As on 11 August 2026, 396 infrastructure projects with a total estimated cost of about ₹18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the Network Planning Group mechanism. Out of these, 256 projects have been sanctioned and 198 projects are under implementation.

The National Logistics Policy has strengthened multimodal logistics efficiency and supply chain integration.

PRAGATI reviewed 382 projects worth over ₹85 lakh crore and resolved 2,958 issues.

Over 4,220 industrial parks are mapped on the India Industrial Land Bank (IILB).

272 plug-and-play industrial parks are operational across the country.

20 industrial smart cities have been approved across 7 industrial corridors.

The BHAVYA scheme has been approved in March 2026 to develop 100 new plug-and-play industrial parks.

BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme has been approved on 24 July 2026, with an outlay of ₹3,030 crore. The scheme will be implemented over five years, from FY2026–27 to FY2030–31.

7 Pradhan Mantri MITRA Parks have been proposed to strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem.

Water, Housing and Urban Development

The infrastructure push extends directly to people’s homes and everyday needs. From tap-water access and affordable housing to urban renewal, these efforts are shaping better living conditions across rural and urban India.

Under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), rural tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore in 2019 to around 15.91 crore households as on 10th August 2026.

JJM 2.0 has been approved in March 2026. The mission has been extended to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore.

Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U), 99.25 lakh houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026. Around 96% of houses under PMAY-U 2.0 are allotted to women.

Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Grameen (PMAY-G), out of the 3.91 crore houses sanctioned, 3.13 crore houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026. Nearly 75% of the houses sanctioned under PMAY-G are either in the name of women or under joint ownership.

The SWAMIH Fund launched in 2019 delivered over 63,000 homes, benefiting around 2.52 lakh people as of June 2026.

Under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0, projects worth about ₹2.79 lakh crore have been sanctioned since 2015.

Under Smart Cities Mission, a total of 7,790 projects worth ₹1,56,257 crore have been completed as of March 2026.

Infrastructure for a Stronger, Future-Ready India

India’s infrastructure journey reflects a decisive shift in the scale and ambition of national development. The focus has moved towards building resilient, high-capacity systems that not only support a fast-growing economy today but also anticipate the needs of tomorrow. Collectively, these initiatives are strengthening the foundation for a more efficient, inclusive, and future-ready India.

headline: Income Tax Department, Mumbai, Inducts 97 Meritorious Sportspersons under Sports Quota
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

Income Tax Department, Mumbai, Inducts 97 Meritorious Sportspersons under Sports Quota

12 AUG 2026 6:14PM by PIB Mumbai

Mumbai, 12 August 2026

The Income Tax Department, Mumbai, has inducted 97 accomplished sportspersons under the sports quota, further strengthening its commitment to recognising sporting excellence and nurturing high-calibre talent in public service. The appointment letters were formally handed over to the newly inducted sportspersons by the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Mumbai, Shri Alok Kumar, at Aayakar Bhawan, Mumbai today.

Applications were invited vide Notification dated 07.01.2026 for 97 vacancies. The recruitment attracted 3,595 applications from sportspersons across various disciplines. Following rigorous scrutiny and evaluation in accordance with the prescribed criteria, 97 candidates were selected on merit.

A significant highlight of the recruitment is that over 80% of the selected sportspersons have represented or participated at the international level, reflecting the exceptional calibre of talent joining the Department.

The notable inductees include Shri Tanush Kotian, an all-rounder of Mumbai Ranji Cricket Team who has also been part of India Test Squad, Shri Abhishek who secured two Gold Medals at the 1st World Yogasana Sports Championship, Ahmedabad (2026), Ms. Tejal Hasabnis, player of Indian Women’s Cricket team, Shri Akash, a para-sportsperson, has won Team Gold Medal at the World Shooting Para Sport World Cup, New Delhi (2024) and Gold Medal at the WSPS World Cup, Al Ain, Dubai (2025).

The recruitment marks a significant milestone in the Income Tax Department’s efforts to promote sporting excellence while providing accomplished athletes an opportunity to serve the nation. Speaking on the occasion, Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Mumbai, Shri Alok Kumar assured the new inductees that they will have every opportunity to continue with their sports practice and competitions. He also stated that the Income Tax Department, Mumbai, expects the newly inducted sportspersons to bring to public service the same discipline, determination and excellence that have distinguished their sporting careers.

As part of the induction programme, the newly recruited sportspersons were briefed on their roles, responsibilities and applicable government rules.
